blocks.text: I can use possessive adjectives and adverbs of position to ask and answer questions about where my and your things are.
You will also practise saying and spotting words with final syllable stress.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: a word that goes before a noun to show ownership or belonging

blocks.text: Say these words aloud. Each one has its stress on the last syllable.
Spanish words ending in consonants other than {-n} and {-s} naturally have final syllable stress. These words don’t need an accent to show the stress.
These words all have final syllable stress too, but they end in a vowel, -n or -s. Say them aloud.
If a word has final syllable stress and ends in {-n} or {-s} or a vowel, there will be an accent on the final vowel.

blocks.label: Why does jardín have an accent but color does not?
blocks.text: ‘Color’ ends in -r, so it doesn’t need an accent to show the final syllable stress. ‘Jardín’ ends in -n, so it does.

blocks.q: All of these words have final syllable stress. Which column does each word belong in?
columns: No accent needed (ends in a consonant other than -n or -s)
Accent needed (ends in -n, -s or a vowel)

blocks.text: Here are some nouns for things you might look for.
‘A pair of trousers’ is **un pantalón**: singular!
These adverbs tell you where something is.
Two more you will meet: **cerca** (near) and **al lado de** (next to).

blocks.q: Match each Spanish adverb of position to its English meaning.

blocks.text: Possessive adjectives go before nouns to show belonging and ownership.

items: {mi} before a singular noun: mi revista (my magazine)
{mis} before a plural noun: mis zapatos (my shoes)
Mi hermana está en casa. (My sister is at home.)
Dejé mis cosas en la escuela. (I left my things at school.)

blocks.text: You can use {mi(s)} with masculine and feminine nouns.

items: {tu} before a singular noun: tu familia (your family)
{tus} before a plural noun: tus amigos (your friends)
Tu botella está en la mesa. (Your bottle is on the table.)
Tus amigas están en clase. (Your friends are in class.)

blocks.text: You can use {tu(s)} with masculine and feminine nouns too.

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: There are two ways of saying ‘my’: mi is for singular nouns, mis is for plural nouns. It is the same for ‘your’: tu and tus.

blocks.q: Choose the correct word to complete each sentence.

items.q: ___ revista está encima de la mesa. (My magazine is on top of the table.)
___ zapatos están debajo de la cama. (My shoes are under the bed.)
___ botellas están cerca de la ventana. (Your bottles are near the window.)
___ amigo está fuera de la tienda. (Your friend is outside the shop.)
___ libros están en clase. (My books are in class.)

blocks.text: Adverbs of location are often followed by **de**. Use de + the (el / la) to link to a noun.

items: Mi móvil está debajo de la cama. (My phone is under the bed.)
Tu amigo está fuera de la tienda. (Your friend is outside the shop.)
Mis fotos están encima del periódico. (My photos are on top of the newspaper.)

rows.note: For a singular masculine noun, de + el changes to del. De + el is always del.

blocks.q: Choose de la or del to complete each sentence.
Which sentence means ‘My papers are inside the box’?
options: Mis papeles están dentro de la caja.
Mi papel está dentro de la caja.
Mis papeles están fuera de la caja.
blocks.why: Papers is plural, so mis. Dentro means inside.

blocks.q: Tus revistas están cerca del teléfono. What does it mean?
options: Your magazine is near the phone.
Your magazines are near the phone.
My magazines are near the phone.
blocks.why: Tus is ‘your’ before a plural noun, and cerca means near.

blocks.q: Which sentence means ‘My money is behind the book’?
options: Mi dinero está detrás del libro.
Mi dinero está delante del libro.
Mis dinero está detrás del libro.
blocks.why: Detrás means behind, and de + el becomes del before el libro.

items: Spanish words ending in consonants other than -n and -s naturally have final syllable stress.
If a word has final syllable stress and ends in -n, -s or a vowel, it has an accent on the final vowel, e.g. habitación.
‘My’: mi before a singular noun, mis before a plural noun. ‘Your’: tu before a singular noun, tus before a plural noun.
Adverbs of location are often followed by de. For a singular masculine noun, de + el changes to del.

blocks.text: Now you can say where your things are, and ask where mine are!

flashcards.back:

flashcards.back:
When it ends in -n, -s or a vowel: the accent goes on the final vowel.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Where are my things? ‘mi’, ‘tu’ and adverbs of position
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a short answer. Some answers are in Spanish and some are in English. Use the rules from the lesson.

questions.prompt: Complete with mi, mis, tu or tus: Busco ___ llaves. (I am looking for my keys.)
questions.explanation: Keys is plural and it is ‘my’, so we use mis.

questions.prompt: Complete with mi, mis, tu or tus: ___ padre está delante del bar. (Your father is in front of the bar.)
questions.explanation: Father is singular and it is ‘your’, so we use tu.

questions.prompt: Complete with de la or del: Tus botellas están cerca ___ jardín.
questions.explanation: El jardín is a singular masculine noun, so de + el becomes del.

questions.prompt: Complete with de la or del: Mi reloj está fuera ___ casa.
questions.explanation: La casa is feminine, so we keep de la.

questions.prompt: The word “pantalon” has final syllable stress and ends in -n. Write it with its accent.
questions.explanation: A word with final syllable stress that ends in -n needs an accent on the final vowel.

questions.prompt: Lucía says: “Está debajo de la mesa.” Where is the book? Answer in English.
questions.explanation: Debajo de means under and la mesa is the table.

questions.prompt: Lucía says: “Están cerca del teléfono.” Where are the magazines? Answer in English.
questions.explanation: Cerca de means near and el teléfono is the phone.

questions.prompt: Write in Spanish: “under” (an adverb of position).
Write in Spanish: “on top” (an adverb of position).
Write in Spanish: “My money is behind the book.”
questions.answer: Mi dinero está detrás del libro.
accepted: Mi dinero está detrás del libro
questions.explanation: Mi (singular noun), detrás (behind) and de + el = del.
